A bag contains $250$ red balls and $150$ white balls. We wish to construct a statistical model for $p^(^)$, the proportion of white balls in a random sample.

Consider the following random samples.

1. $30$ balls are drawn from the bag without replacement.
2. $22$ balls are drawn from the bag with replacement.
3. $15$ balls are drawn from the bag without replacement.

Which of these sampling methods requires a finite population correction factor to be applied to model $p^(^)$ as normal?

*Hint: In all cases, the requirement $np > 5$ and $n(1 - p) > 5$ is satisfied.*

In which of the following situations is it necessary to use a finite population correction factor to adjust the variance so that the sample proportion distribution is approximately normal?

1. A sample of size $n = 40$ from a population of size $N = 1000$ in which $25%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.
2. A sample of size $n = 500$ from a population of size $N = 3000$ in which $80%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.
3. A sample of size $n = 150$ from a population of size $N = 2000$ in which $40%$ of the population has a particular characteristic.

*Hint. In all cases, the requirement $np > 5$ and $n(1 - p) > 5$ is satisfied. You may assume all samples are conducted without replacement.*

:knowledge-point/title: Identifying Situations Where a Correction Factor Is Necessary
